chapters.title: Omnichannel Leads
chapters.subtitle: Work prospects, then convert the ones that qualify

steps.text: A lead is a prospect you have not qualified yet. This video shows how to find and add leads, import a list of them, call and text them, and convert the ones that qualify into contacts, accounts and opportunities.
A purchased list or a trade-show scan is full of people who may never buy. If they were contacts, your customer list would fill with strangers.
Leads are kept apart, but you work them the same way: you can call them, text them, load them as activities and retry them through a subject flow.
When a lead qualifies, you convert it. The lead becomes a contact, and its history moves with it.

chapters.title: The leads list
chapters.subtitle: Status, source and rating at a glance

steps.text: Open Interaction Center, Leads. The list shows the open leads, with each lead's status, rating, company, source and list.
Search with terms. Lead status finds a status by name, Source finds a lead source, and Rating finds hot, warm or cold leads. Here, Rating hot shows the leads to call first.
Other terms are List for the list a lead came in, Owner for the user responsible, and Converted. The phone search terms from the contacts list work here too.
Click New Lead. Besides the name and the contact methods, a lead has a Lead status, a Company, a Lead source, a List, a Rating and a Lead owner.
New leads get the default status. Pick the source from your lead sources, give the list a name, and choose a rating. Then publish.

To load a list, open Content, Import and choose Lead. The Columns Requirements table shows the columns a file can carry: the lead status, source, list, company, rating and owner, next to the name and contact methods.

Skip numbers that already belong to a contact leaves out rows whose number a contact has, so a customer is not called as a stranger. Skip numbers that already belong to an open lead does the same for leads you are still working. Both are on by default.
List name, Lead source, Lead status and Lead owner are given to every new lead whose row does not set its own.

chapters.title: Call and text a lead
chapters.subtitle: The same tools as a contact

steps.text: Everything you do with a contact works on a lead. Open a lead, and use List Activities to see its activities.
Add Activity, Outbound, schedules a call or a text, and Inbound logs one the lead started. Leads can also be loaded as activities, and retried by a subject flow, like any contact.

chapters.title: Convert a lead
chapters.subtitle: Merge or create a contact, an account and an opportunity

steps.text: When a lead qualifies, click Convert on its row. The page says that a contact already has this lead's email, and Merge into is picked, so no duplicate is made.
The contact keeps its own values and only gains what the lead has that it lacks. The account starts from the lead's company, and Create an opportunity records the deal.
Under Activities, choose to move the open activities to the contact, or to cancel them. Click Convert.
For a lead nobody knows yet, choose Create a new contact and its type, create the account, and tick Create an opportunity. Pick the opportunity type, and enter a name, an amount and a close date.
The lead takes the Converted status and becomes read-only. It leaves the Leads list, and the contact has its history.

chapters.title: Convert automatically
chapters.subtitle: Subject flows, the AI and workflows

steps.text: A subject flow can convert a lead when an activity ends with a chosen disposition, for example Qualified. Its Convert Lead action runs before the other actions, so a follow-up activity lands on the new contact.

On an Automatic activity load of a lead type, the AI lead conversion card lets the AI convert a lead that qualified during an automated call or text. It never converts a lead who declined or asked not to be contacted.
With Workflows on, a Lead Converted event starts a workflow when any conversion happens, and a Convert Lead task converts a lead from a workflow.
Three CRM reports follow the leads: the Lead funnel, the Lead conversion by source and list, and the Opportunity pipeline.
Work a purchased list without polluting the contact list.
Follow trade-show leads through statuses, and call the hot ones first.
Convert a qualified lead into a contact, an account and a deal in one step.
Let the AI qualify leads by text or call, and convert the ones that qualify.
Keep prospects as leads, work them like contacts, and convert the ones that qualify, so your contact list holds only real customers. Thanks for watching.
